messages.author: 6873525055e7cfa8
messages.subject: Factor ordering in facet_grid
parts:
Dear ggplot2 experts!

I am trying to plot some bar plot with errorbars ordered according to
two factors using "fill=factor_1" for factor_1 and facet_grid for
factor_2.

The problem that I have is that in the example below the ordering in
one cell of the facet_grid is according to the variable name on the x
axis. However I would like to order the bars according to factor_1 so
that bars of identical colors appear next to each other.

I am aware that I could change the ordering of the factor "name"
plotted on the x axis. However I have the same instances of the
variable "name" in the other cell of the facet grid and I would not
know how to give a different factor level to the same instance of a
variable?

Many thanks for your help & best wishes,
Jokel


Example code:


library(ggplot2)

# create some dummy data
name <- c("Name_1","Name_2","Name_3")
factor_1 <- c("A","B","A","B","A","B")
factor_2 <- c("C","C","C","D","D","D")
mean <- c(1.2,1.5,-2.1,1.9,-0.5,0.9)
sd <- c(0.2,0.5,0.1,0.1,0.25,0.4)
data <-
data.frame(name=name,factor_1=factor_1,factor_2=factor_2,mean=mean,sd=sd)

# plot
ggplot(data,aes(x=name, y=mean, fill=factor_1))
+geom_bar(stat="identity", positio="dodge")
+geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd,ymax=mean+sd))+facet_grid(~factor_2,
scales="free_x", space="free")

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Factor ordering in facet_grid
parts:
Jokel,

Someone may have a cleverer solution, but I'd say you have two choices:

1) For this specific example, relevel your x-axis factor. But this
will apply to both facet panels, which you say is not good.
2) Using viewport, make two entirely separate bar plots, each with the
x-axis ordered however you'd like. This is the solution I would use if
your x-axis ordering needs to change between panels. I can give you
sample code for this if useful.

Ben

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Factor ordering in facet_grid
parts:
Piggybacking on the sample code you've already given, I was thinking
about something like this, which produces a two-panel figure with
differently-ordered x axes.
Ben

# subset into two different data frames and relevel x axis factor
data1 <- subset( data, factor_2=="C" )
data1$name <- relevel( data1$name, "Name_3" )
data2 <- subset( data, factor_2=="D" )
data2$name <- relevel( data2$name, "Name_2" )

# two separate plots, one with no legend or y axis title
panela <- ggplot(data1,aes(x=name, y=mean, fill=factor_1))
+geom_bar(stat="identity", position="dodge")
+geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd,ymax=mean+sd))+opts(legend.position =
"none")
panelb <- ggplot(data2,aes(x=name, y=mean, fill=factor_1))
+geom_bar(stat="identity", position="dodge")
+geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd,ymax=mean+sd))
+opts(axis.title.y=theme_blank())

# draw 'em
grid.newpage()
pushViewport( viewport( layout=grid.layout( 1, 30 ) ) )
vplayout<-function( x, y ) viewport( layout.pos.row=x,
layout.pos.col=y )
print( panela, vp=vplayout( 1, 1:14 ) )
print( panelb, vp=vplayout( 1, 15:30 ) )
